sections.h2: Windsor, two counties and a fast-growing town
sections.html:
Windsor is a home rule town in Northern Colorado that lies in both Weld and Larimer counties. It was platted in 1882 and incorporated on April 2, 1890, and it sits at 4,797 feet across about 26 square miles. The older core runs along State Highway 392, which doubles as Main Street, with the original street grid stretching roughly six blocks north and south of it. The Cache la Poudre River crosses the western and southern sides, and former gravel pits along it now hold lakes with houses and a golf course on their banks.

In the 1990s the town limits were extended west into Larimer County, and the incorporated area west of Interstate 25 now touches Loveland. A house on the Larimer side is recorded and taxed through different county offices than one on the Weld side, so settle the county first.

sections.h2: Growth, housing age and who buys here
sections.html:
The population went from 4,277 in 1980 to 32,716 in the 2020 census, and the 2025 estimate is 43,840. The 2020 count showed 11,807 households and 12,846 housing units, with 8.1% of the units vacant. The median age was 38.2, and 65.9% of households were married-couple households.

That is a family-oriented suburb built mostly in waves of new subdivisions, so two Windsor houses can differ widely in the age of the roof, siding and furnace. Windsor sits between Fort Collins and Greeley, with Loveland close on the west. Many buyers work in one of those cities and choose Windsor for the lot size or newer construction. Most of the town is in the Weld RE-4 School District, and buyers who ask about a school can get the answer from the district.

sections.h2: Hail, tornadoes and the roof question
sections.html:
Hail is the weather event that most often affects a Windsor sale. The town typically sees 6 to 12 hail days a year, and the area where Colorado, Nebraska and Wyoming meet gets more hail than any other place in the country. On May 22, 2008, a tornado hit Windsor and parts of Weld and Larimer counties, with pockets of EF3 damage, estimated winds up to 165 mph and hail as large as baseballs. It caused $193.5 million in damage from about 24,000 auto and homeowner claims.

  • An inspector hired by the buyer will likely flag a roof with old hail damage.
  • A lender or insurer reviewing the house may ask about claim history.
  • Daily temperature swings can top 50 degrees Fahrenheit in spring and fall, which is hard on exterior paint, sealant and concrete.

A cash buyer takes the house as it stands, so a roof worn by hail does not need to be replaced before closing. Owners with storm damage often ask about that.

sections.h2: Building permits and repairs in Windsor
sections.html:
The town runs its own permit desk at 200 N. 11th Street. It is open to the public Monday through Thursday, with online services on Fridays. New building plans are reviewed under the 2024 I-Codes, and the town follows the Colorado Wildfire Resiliency Code. Homeowner handouts cover re-roofs, decks, basement finishes, patio covers and pools.

Permit topicWhat homeowners should know
Contractor licenseNo contractor license is required for work inside the Town
Electrical and plumbingContractors must hold a current State of Colorado license
Permit expirationPermits expire if work does not begin within 180 days or stops for 180 days
Card paymentsA 3% transaction fee applies to credit and debit cards
Inspection requestsRequests by 3:00 p.m. Monday through Thursday are scheduled for the next working day
Permit desk phone970-674-2436

The town's Homeowners Resource Center has HOA information and a wildfire code map, and owners should check that map and ask their insurer about any wildfire-related requirements. If you have open permits or unfinished work, clear it up with the permit technician before a buyer's inspector spots it.

sections.h2: Recording a deed on the Weld County side
sections.html: For a Weld County address, the Clerk and Recorder at 1250 H Street in Greeley records the deed. Recording a letter or legal size document costs $43.00 regardless of page count. Colorado's documentary fee is $.01 per $100 of the sale price when the price is over $500. Both amounts are posted on the county's fee page, and your title company will collect them.

sections.h2: Property taxes when a Windsor house sells
sections.html:
On Weld County parcels, tax for the previous year is due January 1 and can be paid in two equal installments or one full payment. The county's dates are February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half and April 30 for full payment. Interest on late payments begins at 1% and climbs each month.

Title companies confirm that nothing is owed by requesting a Certificate of Taxes Due from the Treasurer. The Treasurer's tax information page has the full schedule.

Notices go to the owner of record. If you have already moved out, confirm the mailing address on file so a bill does not get missed in the middle of a sale.

sections.h2: Listing, selling yourself or taking a cash offer
sections.html:
A Windsor owner has three routes, each with its own timeline. Which one fits depends on the condition of the house and how soon you must close.

  • With an agent: showings, buyer financing and appraisal, and repairs the buyer's inspector asks for.
  • On your own: you handle marketing, contracts and disclosures, and you still need a title company.
  • Cash offer: the buyer purchases as is, and closing runs through a title company on a date that suits you.

Owners who inherited a Windsor house, are behind on payments, have tenants in place or are sitting on hail damage tend to look at the third route. Send the address through the form on this page and we will reply with a written cash offer, with no obligation.

Before you decide, find out which county your parcel is in, collect your latest tax notice, and list any open permits. Those three facts shape every other step, from which office records the deed to what the title company needs from you.

faqs.q: Is Windsor, CO in Weld County or Larimer County?
faqs.a: Both. Windsor lies in Weld and Larimer counties, and the town limits were extended west into Larimer County in the 1990s.

faqs.q: How many people live in Windsor, Colorado?
faqs.a: The census counted 32,716 residents in 2020, and the estimate for 2025 is 43,840.

faqs.q: Does Windsor require a contractor license for repairs before I sell?
faqs.a: No contractor license is required for work inside the Town, although electrical and plumbing contractors must hold a state license. Most projects still need a building permit.

faqs.q: When are Weld County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Tax is due January 1 for the previous year. The county's dates are February 28 for the first half, June 15 for the second half and April 30 for a single full payment.

faqs.q: Can I sell a hail-damaged house in Windsor without replacing the roof?
faqs.a: Yes, if the buyer agrees to take it as is. A cash buyer does not require a new roof first, while a financed buyer's lender or insurer may ask for repairs.
